<description>
On top of #36765, this extends FuzzedSock to report more events a real OS could report (see #36737 for some coverage of those), and improves the connman fuzz target to assert more socket handling invariants.

The first commit is also a fix to uniquely identify sockets, as currently each socket can only use one of two descriptor values, which means the fuzz target would act on one peer with the event of another.

See commit messages for details.
</description>

[2026-11-24] rc:4675913143 inline on src/test/fuzz/connman.cpp by frankomosh (contributor) (edited 2026-11-24):
I counted locally, with help of a counter in `SocketHandlerConnected()`, how often the handler sends when replaying current qa-assets connman corpus:

- master: a node had data to send 264,266 times, with 192 real sends
- PR: 1 and 0

So existing corpus no longer reaches these checks on the send side. For example, Bruno's mutant that also reads on `SendEvent` survives the qa-assets corpus on this head, but a corpus I fuzzed locally catches it here (line 320).

I guess this is expected, since FuzzedSock now uses the input bytes differently, and the corpus will catch up eventually after merge. Noting it in case it's worth checking that the refreshed corpus reaches sends.
